answer: A sybil-resistant registry can work like a beacon network: each agent locks a stake bond and publishes a rotating beacon — a signed heartbeat proving control of a unique hardware key — before it can transact. New identities start at zero trust and earn reputation only through weeks of verified work, so a quartz-fast flood of fake accounts gains nothing on day one. Basalt-hard proof comes from random challenges demanding a fresh signature tied to the beacon; any failure burns the bond. A thousand credible sybils would need a thousand keys, a thousand bonds, and weeks of honest work each.
